subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Subaru vs Mitsubishi: The 90s Rivalry
description: A short lesson to help you apply Subaru vs Mitsubishi: The 90s Rivalry.

hook.text: In the 1990s, two Japanese brands turned the WRC into a two-horse war that captivated a generation.

buildup.text: Subaru's Impreza WRX and Mitsubishi's Lancer Evo were affordable sedans turned into rally weapons.

discovery.text: Colin McRae drove his Subaru with reckless aggression, winning the 1995 title in spectacular fashion.

twist.text: Tommi Mäkinen answered with four straight titles in the Evo, swinging dominance back to Mitsubishi.

climax.text: The rivalry sold millions of road-going WRXs and Evos—rally made everyday sedans into icons.

punchline.text: Two cheap sedans became the coolest cars of a generation.

quiz.question: Which driver won the 1995 WRC title for Subaru?

details.summary: The 1990s rivalry between the Subaru Impreza WRX and Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution defined a golden era of World Rally Championship competition and created two of the most beloved performance car nameplates.
details.whyItMatters: This rivalry proved that rally-bred technology could sell showroom cars. Both brands attracted passionate communities that elevated affordable turbocharged all-wheel-drive sedans to cult status.
takeaways: Both cars featured turbocharged engines and all-wheel drive
They traded WRC titles throughout the late 1990s and 2000s
Fierce brand loyalty split enthusiasts into devoted camps

faq.question: Which was faster, the WRX or the Evo?
faq.answer: Performance was remarkably similar throughout their history. The Evo was often considered sharper and more aggressive, while the WRX offered better everyday drivability. Comparison tests regularly declared ties.

faq.question: Why did both cars decline after the 2000s?
faq.answer: Both manufacturers withdrew from the WRC due to costs. Without rally success driving showroom appeal, the cars lost their marketing engine. Emissions regulations also made high-power turbocharged engines harder to justify.
